item.title: Parkview Enacts Visitor Restrictions With Rise In Respiratory Illnesses
item.description: Increases in respiratory illness activity have resulted in Parkview Health implementing temporary visitor restrictions to protect patients, family and staff.

item.title: Whitko Work-Based Learning Spotlights Two Students
item.description: Whitko Career Academy wants to spotlight Ethan Yates and Catherine Deckena, who serve in a job-share role as front office assistants.

item.title: Lake City Bank Announces Promotion In Agribusiness Banking
item.description: Lake City Bank has announced that Marlee J. Richter has been promoted to assistant vice president, agribusiness portfolio management officer.

item.title: Voelz declares re-election candidacy
item.description: Kosciusko County Prosecuting Attorney J. Brad Voelz declared his candidacy for re-election Friday, Jan. 9.

item.title: House Republicans Roll Out Agenda Focused On Housing, Energy, Deregulation
item.description: Indiana House Republicans on Thursday, Jan. 8 announced a four-bill legislative agenda for the 2026 session focusing on housing affordability, utility costs and deregulation.

item.title: Man Receives Over Two Years In Prison On Child Porn, Voyeurism Charges
item.description: A Kendallville man will serve over two years in prison after possessing over 200 files of child pornography and filming a woman in a dressing room.

item.title: Shelbyville Plan Commission Gives Data Center Unfavorable Recommendation
item.description: A proposed large-scale data center development on Shelbyville’s east side advanced through the City Council but hit a setback days later after the city’s Plan Commission voted against recommending the project.

item.title: Project Ebenezer Raising Funds To Cover Funeral Expenses For Claypool Paramedic
item.description: Project Ebenezer, a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting the mental health and wellness of first responders, is raising funds for the family of a local paramedic who recently passed away.

item.title: ACLU Sues Loogootee For Allegedly Attempting To Block PrideFest Again
item.description: Today, the American Civil Liberties Union of Indiana filed two actions against the City of Loogootee arising from its latest ordinance that would prevent the annual PrideFest from taking place in the city’s Public Square area, in violation of the First Amendment
